classification.difficultyReason: Construct an external altitude and use supplementary-angle sine equality to extend the area formula to an obtuse included angle.

content.prompt: Prove that the formula $\text{Area}=\frac12ab\sin C$ gives the area of a triangle when $C$ is obtuse.

answer.short:
$\text{Area}=\frac12ah=\frac12ab\sin(180^\circ-C)=\frac12ab\sin C$.

Drop a perpendicular to the extension of the base and use the equality of the sines of supplementary angles.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABC$, let $BC=a$, $CA=b$ and $\angle ACB=C$ be obtuse. Extend $BC$ beyond $C$ to $P$ and draw $AP\perp BP$, with $AP=h$.

Since $CP$ and $CB$ point in opposite directions, $\angle ACP=180^\circ-C$. In right-angled triangle $ACP$:
$$\begin{align*}\sin(180^\circ-C)&=\frac{h}{b}\\h&=b\sin(180^\circ-C)\\h&=b\sin C.\end{align*}$$
The last equality uses the fact that supplementary angles have equal sines. Using base $BC=a$ and perpendicular height $h$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle ABC&=\frac12ah\\\text{Area of }\triangle ABC&=\frac12a\bigl(b\sin C\bigr)\\\text{Area of }\triangle ABC&=\frac12ab\sin C.\end{align*}$$
